text: The paper reports that a pattern noted just before this passage occurs in about 80% of the cases where the examiner accepted a false claim and in 45% where it rejected a correct claim. The authors note that in most cases where LM vs LM fails the examinee provided incorrect information to the examiner, which might indicate that it has encoded a large set of wrong facts that are mutually consistent, making it hard for the examiner to detect inconsistencies.
title: In most LM vs LM failures the examinee gives incorrect information
